question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s position as paramount leader remains secure through 2027, with trader consensus at 96% against removal reflecting sustained elite consolidation ahead of the 21st Party Congress. Ongoing anti-corruption purges across the Politburo, Central Military Commission, and senior ranks have eliminated potential rivals without visible factional pushback, while recent leadership gatherings such as the Beidaihe conclave and July 2026 party anniversary events reinforced demands for loyalty and centralized authority. No successor has been elevated, and institutional patterns favor Xi securing a fourth term. Low-probability shifts could still arise from acute health developments, an unprecedented external crisis exposing internal fractures, or sudden elite realignment, though current dynamics show no such catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: The absence of an incumbent or consensus frontrunner after 2024 has produced a wide-open Democratic field, with trader consensus placing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff in a tight cluster at the top. Polling aggregates show more variation, including stronger Harris support in some surveys, yet market pricing indicates traders view the outcome as highly uncertain pending 2026 midterms and candidate announcements that could consolidate or shift support.
